title: Know your types
instructions_md:
## Kinds of values

Every value has a **type**. Three common types:

- `str` is text, such as `"7"`
- `int` is a whole number, such as `7`
- `float` is a number with a decimal point, such as `7.5`

`type()` tells you the type of a value.

```python
print(type("7"))
print(type(7))
print(type(7.5))
```

```text
<class 'str'>
<class 'int'>
<class 'float'>
```

## Your task

Make three variables:

- `title` holds the text `Desert Nights`
- `pages` holds the whole number `96`
- `price` holds the number `2.5`
hints: Only one of the three values needs quotes.
A whole number has no quotes and no decimal point.
Write three lines, each with a name, `=` and a value.

tests.name: `pages` is the whole number `96`
tests.hint: A number inside quotes is text.

tests.name: `price` is the number `2.5`
tests.hint: A number inside quotes is text.
